lanehyst_20260819.decision: Took the SECOND path, with one refinement: the hysteresis lands GATED behind a NEW id 'lanehyst' rather than as an edit to the promoted default. Folding it straight into lanesurv would silently change shipped turbo behavior for every bot with no way to A/B it; a new gate keeps the shipped decision byte-identical and makes the change measurable on its own.
lanehyst_20260819.why_not_the_anchor_path: No safe seam. bots/mode_retreat_generic.lua defines only GetDesire() -- it has NO Think(), so the ENGINE's built-in retreat owns all movement (fountain routing, TP home, shrine, escape items). Holding a position from retreat means authoring a full Think replacement for the most safety-critical mode; and a mode-Think replacement is precisely the wiring the A1 mechanism analysis (l1xpsoak_MECHANISM_20260731) blamed for l1xpsoak's -50 gpm. The only other home, mode_laning_generic's Think replacement, is the condemned design that death-marched 144711 medusa.

Every enemy leaving 1100 releases earlier still (existing early-out). Off the gate the stamp is written but never read -> shipped decision unchanged.
lanehyst_20260819.rationale_c: Schmitt trigger on a blinking binary control signal. GetEstimatedDamageToTarget is mana/cooldown-aware, so a nuke coming off cooldown / an enemy stepping 20u past 1100 / a mana tick flips the decision between adjacent frames; a retreat that wins the desire auction for one frame and loses it the next issues a move order and cancels it -- neither retreating nor laning. The codebase already applies the same medicine on the l1kite path (bot.laneKiteUntil kite-lock, added for watched 181046 CK flapping).
lanehyst_20260819.anti_parking_brake: TIME-BOUNDED on purpose, unlike the l1xpsoak hold (which released only on state change and could hold indefinitely). 2.0s can smooth a blink; it cannot become the force-passivity failure mode that rejected lf_recover / corefarm / l1xpsoak wave 1.

But GetDesire() pipes the helper's value through CapForLanePush, which soft-ceils any desire >0.9 to 0.72 whenever J.IsInLaningPhase() or J.IsPushing(). Both J.ShouldInitiateLaneKill and J.ShouldSupportComboKill HARD-REQUIRE J.IsInLaningPhase(), so the cap's trigger condition is a strict SUPERSET of the two branches' entire domain: the 0.92 literal was unreachable on every frame they could possibly fire, the effective bid (0.72) landed BELOW the 0.75 it was picked to beat, and the effective bid was NON-MONOTONIC in HP (healthy core 0.72, half-HP core ~0.90). Neither branch set bDefensiveCollapse, and the existing 'divecap' exemption is both collapse-only and itself unarmed.
lanekill_cap_fix_20260819.same_family_as: GH #29 (retreat guard chain priority inversion). Both are 'the desire the author wrote is not the desire the engine sees' -- an author-intended relative ordering silently destroyed by a downstream transform. Worth treating as a recurring class, not two incidents.
lanekill_cap_fix_20260819.fix: New frame flag bLaneKillCommit (mirrors the existing bDefensiveCollapse pattern), reset each frame in GetDesireHelper, raised inside the two lane-kill branches, and exempted in _divecap_CapForLanePush (4th param). No extra soak gate on the exemption: the flag is only reachable from inside branches already gated on 'l1trade'/'l5combo'. Cap behavior for every other path is byte-identical. The 0.92 literal was KEPT (not lowered to <=0.9): bidding just under a cap threshold is the same implicit coupling that produced this bug.
lanekill_cap_fix_20260819.shipped_default_impact: NONE. Both raise sites sit inside branches whose helpers return nil unless turbo AND the soak candidate is armed, so with all gates off the flag is never raised and CapForLanePush is unchanged. Pinned by a source-level containment test, not just by inspection.
lanekill_cap_fix_20260819.validation: tests/test_lanekill_bid_reachable.lua (6 tests): drives the REAL global GetDesire() end-to-end (not the trigger helpers) and asserts the engine receives 0.92 and that it exceeds 0.75, for both ids; asserts the effective bid is monotone non-decreasing over a 21-point HP sweep; asserts a non-exempt roam desire is still capped to 0.72; and asserts at the source level that 'bLaneKillCommit = true' occurs exactly twice, each structurally inside a gated trigger branch carrying the ShouldReleaseLaneCommit guard. MUTATION-CHECKED twice: deleting the exemption (byte-equivalent to the pre-fix source) fails 4 tests including both end-to-end ones reporting the 0.72 clobber; deleting one raise site fails exactly the 2 relevant tests. Full suite 396/396, luacheck 0 warnings.
lanekill_cap_fix_20260819.coverage_gap_it_closed: GH #31 sec.4 was right about the root cause of survival: tests/test_l1_trade.lua and tests/test_l5_combo.lua only ever asserted the TRIGGER (J.Should*), and tests/test_divecap_gate.lua only the cap predicate in isolation. Nothing asserted their COMPOSITION -- the number the engine actually receives. That composition is now covered. Any future branch in this file whose comment reasons about a relative desire ordering should get the same end-to-end assertion.
lanekill_cap_fix_20260819.why_no_real_frame_fixture: The two helpers' decisive gates (lethality: combined castable burst >= target HP + 4s regen; self-risk: their burst vs mine) both run GetEstimatedDamageToTarget, which the behav dumper does not record (GH #27, GH #28 both flag the same gap). So no archived frame can be replayed into a state where the trigger provably returns non-nil -- a fixture could pin the geometry but not the firing. The defect is also a domain-wide arithmetic fact (cap domain superset of branch domain), which a single frame cannot express: the monotonicity sweep is the honest form of that claim.
lanekill_cap_fix_20260819.READING_IMPACT_on_prior_batch_data: IMPORTANT for whoever reads the 14-id 4-seed -34.59 gpm residual: l1trade and l5combo were armed in that wave but were bidding 0.72, never the designed 0.92. Their contribution to that number is NOT a measurement of the rule as designed -- they were not inert (0.72 still competes) but they were not the rule either. Their prior 'evidence insufficient / undetermined' status is VOID, not carried forward. After this fix both ids are behaviorally NEW and have never been measured at their designed bid.
lanekill_cap_fix_20260819.bisect_guidance: Kept both ids ARMED rather than retiring them (unlike creeppull/pullcamp/l1xpsoak, whose condition (a) was structurally unprovable -- here the fix makes (a) provable). The wave13 20260723 failure mode (a 0.95 bid pinning bots into losing trades) is guarded by J.ShouldReleaseLaneCommit (self-release when the committing bot is the one dying) plus the once-per-engagement 4s commit lock, both already present and both required by the new source-level test. capmono_20260819.source: strategy work unit 2026-08-19T09:5xZ, the other half of GH #31 (director fixed the lane-kill side at 09:04Z by EXEMPTING those two branches; this covers the branches that stay capped)
capmono_20260819.defect: bots/mode_team_roam_generic.lua _divecap_CapForLanePush calls itself a 'soft ceiling' but implements a CLIFF: only desire > 0.9 is pulled down, and it lands at 0.72 -- BELOW the whole (0.72, 0.9] band that passes untouched. Every branch still routed through it bids RemapValClamped(J.GetHP(bot), 0, 0.5 or 0.6, BOT_MODE_DESIRE_NONE, 0.98) -- ConsiderHelpWhenCoreIsTargeted, ConsiderHelpAlly, J.ShouldPunishDive ('punish'), J.ShouldPunishOverchase ('overchase', ARMED in test_set.md). So the effective bid is NON-MONOTONIC in HP with its maximum at ~46% HP: full HP -> 0.72 (loses to the promoted lanesurv retreat at 0.75), 43% HP -> 0.843 (BEATS it), 36% HP -> 0.71 (loses again). The hero least able to survive a collapse is the only one who wins the desire auction and gets pinned into it -- and unlike the lane-kill branches, none of these four carries J.ShouldReleaseLaneCommit to escape.
capmono_20260819.change: Gated turbo + J.IsSoakCandidate('capmono'): inside the existing `if J.IsInLaningPhase() or J.IsPushing(hBot)` block, replace the cliff with a genuine ceiling, `if desire > 0.72 then return 0.72 end; return desire`. Off the gate the cliff line runs unchanged -- shipped defaults byte-for-byte identical. The GH #31 lane-kill exemption and the (still gated) 'divecap' collapse exemption both sit ABOVE this and are unaffected.
capmono_20260819.rationale_c: Two independent grounds. (1) Internal precedent: this is the same defect the director just fixed for l1trade/l5combo in GH #31 and the same shape as the wave13 dossier finding ('the old 0.95 bid outbid the PROMOTED lanesurv retreat (0.75) and pinned bots into losing trades'). (2) Standard strategy: commitment to a fight should rise with your ability to survive it, never fall -- a support at 43% HP collapsing HARDER than the same support at full HP is backwards under any Dota fight-commitment model. Monotonicity of an effective bid in HP is a shape property, not a tuning choice.
capmono_20260819.conservatism: The armed path can only ever LOWER a desire (pure min against the ceiling that is already there). That is why it is separable from 'divecap': divecap UNCAPS collapses during laning and was deliberately left dark because it could cause over-commitment; capmono cannot, by construction. One lever only -- the ceiling VALUE (0.72) is untouched.
capmono_20260819.validation: tests/test_capmono_ceiling.lua -- 12 cases on the real frame f_222428_lion_lich_burst (Lion 354/823 = 43.0% hp at t=314.0, Lich 660u + Axe 800u, no ally within 2200; ground truth from the replay: Lich dealt 436 damage, Lion died 6.9s later). The frame is genuinely inside turbo laning (t < 480) so the cap is live on it, and J.ShouldRetreatLaneBurst (PROMOTED lanesurv, bids 0.75) genuinely fires on it -- asserted, not assumed. Cases: real-frame cap-live + retreat-fires; 43% bid 0.843 > 0.75 (the bug, on the frame that killed him); same frame at full HP bids 0.72 < 0.75 (the inversion, straddling the retreat bid); armed -> 0.72 < 0.75 so the retreat wins; a 21-point HP sweep driven through the REAL global GetDesire() (only the trigger J.ShouldPunishOverchase is forced, to the real Lich handle) asserting monotonicity armed AND asserting the shipped default is still non-monotonic (so the test retires itself if the cliff ever goes); shipped cap unchanged at 0.98/0.95/0.90/0.84/0.60; armed path never raises a desire; the GH #31 exemption still wins; scoped to laning/pushing; turbo-only.
capmono_20260819.mutation_tests: Two. Deleting the gated branch (= pre-fix source) fails exactly the 3 armed assertions, and the monotonicity message prints the real inversion (bid fell 0.881 -> 0.72 as HP rose to 0.5). Forcing the gate always-on fails exactly the 5 shipped-default/defect-present assertions. 408/408 tests, luacheck bots game 0 warnings.
capmono_20260819.scope_note: Two of the four affected branches (ConsiderHelpWhenCoreIsTargeted, ConsiderHelpAlly) are SHIPPED defaults, not gated -- which is why this had to land behind its own gate rather than as a direct edit. Arming 'capmono' therefore changes shipped help-ally/help-core collapse behavior in the 44-55% HP band as well as the two punish ids; that breadth is deliberate (the defect is in the shared transform, not in any one branch) and is the main thing a batch read should watch.

tpdying_20260819.source: strategy work unit 2026-08-19T11:5xZ, backlog item 8 (the 'final bid reachability' sweep). First id audited from the group's untouched list: tpcommit. GH #35.
tpdying_20260819.defect: J.GetTpCommitDefendDesire pins a fresh TP responder in the answered lane's DEFEND mode with a 0.85 floor, and releases the pin on `J.GetHP(bot) < 0.40 or J.ShouldRetreatLaneBurst(bot)`. The second clause is the ANTICIPATORY one -- the reason the release works at all, since a lander who waits for 40% has already eaten the burst -- but J.ShouldRetreatLaneBurst hard-requires J.IsInLaningPhase() on its third line. The floor is only reachable from the two response-TP branches (J.GetRescueTpTarget / J.ShouldTpSupportTowerFight), which require level 6+ and a >3500u trip, so the frames it actually pins are overwhelmingly POST-laning. There the release degrades to the numeric clause alone: the pin holds until the lander is ALREADY losing. That is the same 'ground down in place' shape (wave12 dossier mechanism D, ~6/24 landing deaths) the release was written against, minus the half that made it work. Same family as GH #29 / #31 / #32: a condition whose DOMAIN does not cover its branch's domain.
tpdying_20260819.change: New pure predicate J.IsIncomingBurstLethal(bot, nWindow) -- the same mana/cd-aware estimator J.ShouldRetreatLaneBurst runs over the enemies within 1100, without the laning gate; true when their castable burst already covers the bot's current health. Consumed by ONE new gated release clause inside J.GetTpCommitDefendDesire, immediately after the shipped release: `if J.IsSoakCandidate('tpdying') and J.IsIncomingBurstLethal(bot, 3.0) then release end`. Reachable only inside the existing 'tpcommit' gate, so both shipped play AND today's armed-tpcommit behavior are byte-identical until 'tpdying' is armed.
tpdying_20260819.rationale_c: Two grounds. (1) Internal: the shipped release's own comment states the contract -- '丢失了动手机会才会走', a lander who is dying has lost the chance. This restores that contract in the domain the floor runs in; nothing new is claimed. (2) Standard strategy: whether to hold a contested spot is decided on incoming damage vs effective HP, not on a fixed HP percentage -- a 100% HP support inside a lethal combo should leave, a 45% HP hero out of range should not. Anticipating burst rather than reacting to an HP threshold is the same principle the PROMOTED lanesurv rule already ships on.
tpdying_20260819.conservatism: The armed path can only RELEASE a pin (return nil sooner) -- it can never raise or create one, and it cannot fire at all unless 'tpcommit' is armed too. Structurally it cannot add commitment, the same separability argument that let capmono ship ahead of divecap. One lever: the floor VALUE (0.85), the 12s window and the shipped release are all untouched.
tpdying_20260819.validation: tests/test_tpcommit_release_domain.lua -- 9 cases on the real frame f_182552_warlock_ult_hoard (t=626.0 / 10:26; Warlock 546/1022 = 53.4% HP; sniper 1008u away; replay ground truth: sniper dealt 669 into that 546 pool, died_after = 2.3s). Both premises are ASSERTED, not assumed: IsInLaningPhase() is false at t=626 (past turbo's 10-min soft end whatever the net worth) so the anticipatory clause is structurally dead, and GetHP > 0.40 so the numeric clause is silent. Every desire assertion drives the REAL mode files -- bots/mode_defend_tower_mid_generic.lua and bots/mode_retreat_generic.lua GetDesire() -- per the test_set.md 0b rule: armed tpcommit -> defend bids 0.85 vs retreat -0.05 on the frame the hero was being killed; shipped-only -> 0.1; +tpdying -> back to 0.1. Containment: tpdying alone (no tpcommit) changes nothing, a survivable 100-damage burst keeps the pin, non-turbo keeps the pin. Reverse assertion: the shipped release is still exactly the laning-only pair (39% releases, 41% does not), so the test self-reports as obsolete if anyone makes the shipped release domain-correct.
tpdying_20260819.mutation_tests: Two. Deleting the gated clause (= pre-fix source) fails exactly the one armed assertion, printing the real pin (got 0.85). Forcing the gate always-on fails exactly the 2 shipped-behavior assertions. 427/427 tests, luacheck bots game 0 warnings.
tpdying_20260819.tooling_note: Getting a FINAL-BID assertion out of the TP/defend family needed four mock-fidelity repairs, all reusable by the whole team: BOT_MODE_DESIRE_* / BOT_ACTION_DESIRE_* now carry their real 0..1 values instead of the auto-const metatable's arbitrary ids (before this, Defend.GetDefendDesire returned 1008/1009 and no cross-mode bid comparison was meaningful); mock Vector gained Normalized/Length/Length2D/Dot; handle-returning getters (GetAttackTarget/GetTarget/GetCurrentActionTarget) answer nil rather than 0, and NumModifiers answers 0; the fixture loader wires the REAL per-team unit:DistanceFromFountain() from the shipped fountain constants. Net effect: bots/mode_defend_tower_*_generic.lua and bots/mode_retreat_generic.lua can now be dofile'd and their GetDesire() driven on a real frame. All 418 pre-existing tests stayed green through the change.

axebuyblink_20260819.fix: BlinkFirstBuild(tList) in bots/BotLib/hero_axe.lua rebuilds the pos_1 and pos_3 lists FROM the shipped ones by moving item_blink to index 2 (straight after the starting-items bundle, which carries the boots) and leaving every other item in its relative order. Applied only when J.IsModeTurbo() and J.IsSoakCandidate('axebuyblink'); otherwise the shipped tables are untouched, so gate-off behaviour is byte-identical. Derived rather than duplicated so the shipped and candidate orders cannot drift apart.
axebuyblink_20260819.theory: Blink Dagger is the standard first big item on Axe in every mainstream build: it is not a chase or escape tool but the delivery system for Berserker's Call, and the rest of the kit is priced off the enemies the Call pins. Vanguard/Crimson Guard buy survivability but no initiation, so a melee initiator holding them can still only fight what walks into him. Turbo compresses the game to ~11 minutes, which makes a 3.6k defensive item bought before the 2.25k enabler a strictly worse ordering than in normal mode. Reachability is measured, not assumed: from Axe's own gold curves, blink bought straight after boots would have landed at 558.5 / 479.4 / 584.5s and never in the fourth game -- 3 of 4 games gain a blink with 100-240s of a decisive turbo game left, against 0 of 4 today.
axebuyblink_20260819.validation: tests/test_axe_blink_build.lua, 10 cases: gate-off pos_3 and pos_1 asserted byte-for-byte against transcribed copies of the shipped lists; armed-but-normal-mode unchanged (turbo-only); a DIFFERENT armed candidate ('wkbuild') unchanged; armed turbo puts blink at index 2 for pos_3 and pos_1 with a multiset-equality check (nothing added or dropped) and a subsequence check (every non-blink item keeps its relative order); the aliased positions pos_2/pos_4/pos_5 follow their base list armed and stay shipped unarmed; the reachability arithmetic evaluated against the list actually under test (it first asserts that ONLY the starting outfit precedes blink, so inserting anything there fails the test rather than silently invalidating the measurement); and a tripwire pinning the shipped pos_3 indices the measurement was taken against. FOUR mutation tests all caught: removing the gate (6 fails), dropping the turbo check (1), landing blink third instead of second (4), dropping blink instead of moving it (4). luacheck 0 warnings; full suite 499/499 green (baseline 489 + 10 new).
